origin.description: Plots Pen's parade of a numeric vector.
origin.usage:
Pen(x, n = rep(1, length(x)), group = NULL,
  scaled = TRUE, abline = TRUE, add = FALSE, segments = NULL,
  main = "Pen's Parade", ylab = NULL, xlab = NULL,
  col = NULL, lwd = NULL, las = 1, fill = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector of non-negative values.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Frequencies or weights, the same length as x. The default is a one for every entry.

arguments.name: group
arguments.text: A factor of group labels, the same length as x. See details.

arguments.name: scaled
arguments.text: If TRUE, divide the parade by mean(x).

arguments.name: abline
arguments.text: If TRUE, draw a horizontal line at the mean of the plotted heights.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: If TRUE, add the parade to an existing plot instead of opening a new one.

arguments.name: segments
arguments.text: If TRUE, draw histogram-like bars. The default is TRUE when group is given and FALSE otherwise.

arguments.name: col
arguments.text: One color, or a vector of colors, for the curve or the bar borders.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: One color, or a vector of colors, for the area under the curve or the bar interiors.

arguments.name: xlab, ylab
arguments.text: Axis labels. Defaults depend on scaled and on whether every weight equals 1.

arguments.name: main, lwd, las, ...
arguments.text: Title, line width, horizontal tick labels, and further plot arguments.

origin.details: Pen's parade is the inverse distribution function, standardized by mean(x) when scaled is TRUE. Missing values in x are dropped, the rest are ordered, and the horizontal axis is the cumulative share of the weights. With a grouping factor the default chart is a stack of gray bars, one shade per level. Without a fill the default is a thick blue step. Those choices are only defaults.

translation.description: Draws Pen's parade of a numeric sample.
translation.usage: Pen(x, n=None, group=None, scaled=True, abline=True, add=False, segments=None, main="Pen's Parade", ylabel=None, xlabel=None, color=None, lwd=None, fill=None, ax=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: One-dimensional numeric sample. Missing values are dropped. Entries are expected to be non-negative.

arguments.name: n
arguments.text: Frequencies aligned with x. None uses a one for every original entry, including positions later dropped because x is missing.

arguments.name: group
arguments.text: Labels aligned with x. Levels are the sorted unique labels, as with R's as.factor.

arguments.name: scaled
arguments.text: If true, divide the ordered values by their unweighted mean.

arguments.name: abline
arguments.text: If true, and add is false, draw a dotted horizontal line at the mean of the plotted heights.

arguments.name: add
arguments.text: If true, draw on the current axes without replacing the title, labels, or limits, and without the mean line.

arguments.name: segments
arguments.text: If true, draw histogram-like bars. None means true when group is given and false otherwise.

arguments.name: color
arguments.text: Color or colors for the step or the bar borders. This is col in R. A vector is recycled and then ordered with the data when bars are drawn.

arguments.name: fill
arguments.text: Fill color or colors. With groups and no fill, bars use Matplotlib grays spaced from 0.3 to 0.9.

arguments.name: ylabel, xlabel
arguments.text: Axis labels. None selects a label that depends on scaled and on whether every weight is 1.

arguments.name: main, lwd, ax
arguments.text: Title, line width, and the axes to draw on. None for ax opens a new figure unless add is true.

translation.details: The parade orders x and walks the cumulative weight share. Scaling uses the unweighted mean of the ordered values, matching Pen in R, not a mean weighted by n. Bars are Matplotlib bars. The ungrouped chart is a step line that starts at the origin, rises to the first height, and stays flat across each class. The mean line is dotted and is omitted when add is true.
translation.value: A dict with p (cumulative shares, including 0), y (ordered heights, scaled when requested), and mean (the mean-line height).
